page.factions.s60_l1: Choose your army by atmosphere, but also by what costume you can prepare.
page.factions.s60_l2: Every participant has a costume duty for the whole event.
page.factions.s60_l3: The costume doesn’t have to be perfect, but it must be thematic and non-distracting.
page.factions.s60_l4: Weapons must be safe, approved and visually fitting for the world of Middle-earth.

page.factions.s60_l7: If you don’t want to fight, you can come as non-combatant escort, atmospheric character, photographer, helper or parent.
page.factions.s60_l8_pre: If you’re not sure what to choose, start with

page.factions.role_t_hobiti: Second breakfast, a pipe and a different point of view.

page.factions.role_l_hobiti_3: suitable for the inn, market, NPC roles,

page.factions.role_t_photog: Capturing the story yes. Getting in the way of the game no.
page.factions.role_d_photog: Photographers and videographers must comply with the costume duty and movement rules in the play space.
page.factions.role_t_stalls: Crafts, market and things for Middle-earth.
page.factions.role_d_stalls: Sellers of costumes, fabrics, leather accessories, jewellery, LARP weapons and other thematic gear. The stall is part of the market and the campsite.
page.factions.role_l_stalls_2: staffing in costume or unobtrusive clothing,
page.factions.role_t_helpers: Without you the camp wouldn’t stand. Without us, neither.
page.factions.role_d_helpers_pre: We’re looking for people who want to help with organisation — registration, weapon checks, the children’s game, camp programme, facilities. The reward is usually
page.factions.role_d_helpers_post: , good vibes and the respect of the community.
page.factions.role_l_helpers_2: you can help with a specific area,
page.factions.role_l_helpers_3: write to us in advance about what you enjoy,
page.factions.role_d_orgs: The team that prepares, organises and runs the whole weekend. You’ll find contacts, team roles and a few words about the people who make it all happen.
page.factions.role_l_orgs_1: you cannot sign up to be an organiser,
page.factions.role_l_orgs_2: the team is built by long-term agreement,
page.factions.role_l_orgs_4: want to be more involved in the community? Get in touch.

page.factions.kids_p2: The children’s game runs separately from the main battle and is for children who want to live their own story in Middle-earth.

page.world_intro.meta_title: Introduction to the world of Middle-earth — Eru, Valar, Arda
page.world_intro.description: A brief introduction to the cosmology of Tolkien’s world: Eru Ilúvatar, Ainur, Valar, Maiar, Arda, Eä and the origin of evil in Melkor and Sauron.
page.world_intro.title: Introduction to the world
page.world_intro.subtitle: Before the horns sound and the armies clash, it’s worth knowing how the world even came to be.
page.world_intro.summary: The world of Middle-earth is part of a larger whole — Arda. It was created by Eru alone through the music of the Ainur. The mightiest Ainur, the Valar, watch over Arda from the distant West. The lesser Maiar serve as messengers and warriors. From one of the Ainur, Melkor, evil arose; from his servant Sauron then came the Shadow that runs through the whole known story.
page.world_intro.eru_p1_pre: At the beginning of all stands
page.world_intro.eru_p1_post: — the One, father of all. He is not lord of one nation or one place; he is the source of the music that gave the world its shape and of the fate that flows through it.
page.world_intro.eru_p2: In Tolkien’s conception Eru never intervenes in the affairs of Middle-earth directly. When evil reaches a point that requires intervention from above, he does it through the Valar, the Maiar or through fate — what sometimes looks like coincidence but never quite is.
page.world_intro.h_ainur: The Ainur and the Great Music
page.world_intro.ainur_p1_pre: Before the world Eru created the
page.world_intro.ainur_p1_mid: — spiritual beings to help him. Together they sang a great Music (
page.world_intro.ainur_p1_mid2: ), in which the future story of Arda was set out. From this music the world was then established by the word
page.world_intro.ainur_p2_pre: Some of the Ainur descended into the world to watch over it. From them came two groups:
page.world_intro.ainur_p2_mid: — the mightiest, something like gods of being — and the
page.world_intro.ainur_p2_post: , their servants, messengers, warriors. Among the Maiar are both Sauron and those who stand against him: Gandalf, Saruman, Radagast — who come to Middle-earth in the form of the Istari.
page.world_intro.arda_p1_pre: The world in which the story of The Lord of the Rings takes place is not called “Middle-earth”. Middle-earth is just
page.world_intro.arda_p1_mid2: . In the west of Arda lies
page.world_intro.arda_p1_post: , the unreachable land of the Valar. Between them is the Great Sea.
page.world_intro.arda_p2: Middle-earth itself is long. Forodwaith stretches across its north, Harad along its south; in the east lie lands beyond the sight of its known powers. The story of The Lord of the Rings takes place only in its western strip — from the Grey Havens and the Shire in the north-west to Mordor and Harad in the south-east.
page.world_intro.evil_p1_pre: Among the Ainur there was one —
page.world_intro.evil_p1_mid: — who wanted to set himself above the others. In the music he played not harmony but his own song; in Arda he then began to spoil what the Valar were creating. Unlike the beings of other mythologies, here evil does not stand on its own but is
page.world_intro.evil_p1_post: — it has no power of its own to create, it can only blight and muddy.
page.world_intro.evil_p2_pre: After long wars Melkor fell, was bound and led out of the world. But his shadow did not vanish. His first servant,
page.world_intro.evil_p2_post: , remained, and the whole later story — the entire Second and Third Age — is a continuation of this old war under another name.
page.world_intro.h_races: Peoples and the Children of Eru
page.world_intro.races_p1_pre: Eru brought two main races to Arda. First awoke the
page.world_intro.races_p1_mid: — the elves. After them came the
page.world_intro.races_p1_post: — humans. Dwarves, with their unusual origin, came from Aulë’s work and Eru’s acceptance; the Ents were then awakened by Yavanna to protect the trees.
page.world_intro.races_p2_pre: Orcs, trolls and other creatures of the Shadow are, in Tolkien’s conception, the result of
page.world_intro.races_p2_post: — Melkor cannot create them, he only twists what already exists. This logic matters for understanding their behaviour in the world.
page.world_intro.alert_p_pre: Some parts of the cosmology are more an interesting backdrop than something you need for the game. For practical event participation you don’t need to know the whole Silmarillion — it’s enough to know that the world
page.world_intro.alert_p_strong: is not created as an even game between two sides
page.world_intro.alert_p_post: , but as a reflection of the struggle between order and its corruption. The atmosphere we try to keep this year flows from that.
page.world_intro.footnote: Texts are paraphrased, without direct quotations from Tolkien’s books. Where our game conception differs from the canon, we use the marker “in our game conception”.
page.world.meta_title: Middle-earth world — peoples, places and history
page.world.description: An overview of Middle-earth lore for The Lord of the Rings event: peoples, kingdoms, armies, timeline, geography and thematic lore for players and newcomers.
page.world.title: Middle-earth world
page.world.subtitle: Lore, peoples, places and the history of the world in which our game takes place.
page.world.intro: The Lord of the Rings is set in a world inspired by Tolkien’s Middle-earth. This part of the website helps you understand the wider historical, cultural and geographic background — who you’ll meet in the game, who has scores with whom, where they come from, what you wear and what you talk about in camp.
page.world.alert_lore_pre: You don’t need to know all of this to come. This part is for those who want to better understand their costume, army, places and history. For participation itself, the most important things are
page.world.h_what: What you’ll find in this section
page.world.cat1_desc: Eru, Ainur, Valar, Maiar, Arda, Eä — the cosmology that everything flows from.
page.world.cat2_desc: Elves, dwarves, Dúnedain, Rohirrim, Haradrim, Umbarians, Easterlings, orcs.
page.world.cat3_desc: Three layers: a quick one for newcomers, expanded Third Age, detail of the War of the Ring.
page.world.cat4_desc: Rohan, the Misty Mountains, forests and elven realms, fortresses, Eriador, Mordor, the south.
page.world.cat5_desc: Political and power overview — who ruled what, when and how it ended.
page.world.cat6_desc: Companies from our LARP’s history — Glóin’s corps, the Garrison of the Deep, the Black Sun.
page.world.cat7_desc: Middle-earth, Valar, Númenor, Rings of Power, Nazgûl and other terms in alphabetical order.
page.world.kanon_p: Some parts of our lore content go hand in hand with Tolkien’s books. Others are our interpretation — for the needs of the game, the year’s story or the dramaturgy of a specific weekend. In the texts we use tags so it’s clear what is what:
page.world.tag1_desc: In line with the books and appendices.
page.world.tag2_desc: Our LARP interpretation — doesn’t have to fit the canon literally.
page.world.tag3_desc: Helps with the costume and atmosphere.
page.world.tag5_desc: Doesn’t change game rules; it’s the lore layer.
page.world.alert_rules_strong: does not determine the game rules
page.world.alert_rules_mid1: . For participation in PP, what applies is what is in the sections
page.world.alert_rules_post: . Even if a people plays a certain role in the books, our game rules and registration categories apply at the event.
page.world.h_year: How Middle-earth maps to our year
page.world.year_p1: The Lord of the Rings is a LARP interpretation of Tolkien’s world. We start from the atmosphere, peoples and main conflicts, but we keep the freedom for our own story and our own decisions of characters. It is not a literal transfer of the books or the film — it is a weekend in which players share a world together and create another part of its story.
page.world.year_p2_pre: If you’re curious about the specific year in which our edition takes place, you’ll find it in the
page.world.cta_h: Want to play one of the peoples?
page.world.cta_p: Enjoying the lore? Have a look at the practical information about the armies — what the costume looks like, what the combat style is, who the army suits and how to sign up.
page.world.footer_note: This part of the website serves as a fan and game guide. It is not an official encyclopaedia of Tolkien’s work. We write the texts in our own words, without direct quotations from the books, the film or wikis.

page.practical.card.misto.title: Location & travel
page.practical.card.misto.desc: Camp near Brno — registered participants receive exact GPS 14 days before the event. About a 20-minute walk from the bus stop.

page.practical.card.strava.desc: We do not directly arrange catering. There will be a partnered pub on site — U Zeleného draka — that can serve meals. Your own food supply, plate, cutlery and mug recommended.

page.practical.card.bezpecnost.title: Safety
page.practical.card.bezpecnost.desc: Permanent medic. Everything goes through a safety check (cek). Rule of zero — STOP halts the game.

page.practical.pack.5: Your own mess kit (plate, cutlery, mug)
page.practical.har.title: Weekend schedule
page.practical.har.subtitle: It’s not just the Saturday battle. The event starts on Thursday and ends on Sunday.
page.practical.har.thu_what: Arrival, camp setup, registration, first meetings, evening fire
page.practical.har.fri_what: Camp play, side programme, children’s game, market, arenas

page.practical.thu.p1: Thursday opens the weekend. The first participants arrive, the camp is set up, registration takes place and people start settling into their armies and warbands.
page.practical.thu.p2: Thursday is ideal for those who want to arrive at a calm pace, pitch a tent, meet others and tune into the weekend without Saturday’s rush.

page.practical.thu.li3: meeting your army, evening fire and camp atmosphere.
page.practical.fri.h3: Friday 21 Aug — The camp comes alive
page.practical.fri.p1: Friday isn’t the main battle. It’s the day the camp turns into a lively place full of preparations, programme, meetings and smaller games. Suitable for newcomers, families with children, escorts, photographers.
page.practical.fri.li1: play in the camp, side programme,
page.practical.fri.li2: children’s game, market and stalls, arenas,
page.practical.sat.p1: Saturday is the main day. Muster takes place, rules are explained, latecomers register, weapons and costumes are checked, armies are summoned and the main game / battle takes place.
page.practical.sat.li2: assignment of lives based on costume,
page.practical.sat.li3: armies marching out, main in-game clashes,
page.practical.sun.p1: On Sunday camp is packed up, the area is cleaned and participants head home. Help with the cleanup is welcome and goes a long way to making sure only flattened grass is left after the event.
page.practical.sun.li1: packing the tent, cleaning the camp,
page.practical.sun.li2: taking out rubbish, checking the area,
page.practical.har.alert_strong: It’s not just the Saturday battle.
page.practical.har.alert_post: If you can, come for the whole weekend — it’s easier to get into your army, meet people, prepare your gear and experience the atmosphere that simply doesn’t fit into Saturday alone.

page.practical.eq.alert_warn_body: Every participant goes through a mandatory weapon and costume safety check on arrival. Without approval you can’t play.

page.practical.food.title: Food & drink
page.practical.food.p1: As organisers we don’t directly provide catering. Each participant is responsible for their own food and drink.
page.practical.food.p2_pre: To make the stay more comfortable, we’re arranging the on-site pub
page.practical.food.p2_post: , where you’ll be able to buy food and drink from their menu and operating capacity.
page.practical.food.p3: We recommend bringing your own basic reserve of food and drink, especially if:
page.practical.food.li5: you know that without a second dinner you turn into an orc.
page.practical.food.note: Drinking water will be available on site from a delivered tank. Don’t expect showers, electricity or the comfort of the inn at Rivendell — we’re on a meadow, in nature.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.subheading: The most common questions before the event
faq.q1: Is the event suitable for newcomers?
faq.a1: Yes — we run a programme for complete newcomers including intro workshops, rule briefings and the option to join one of the bigger groups.
faq.q2: What do I need for a costume?
faq.a2: A basic costume must match the Middle-earth theme of your chosen army. Specific requirements are in the Armies section of your side. If you don’t have a costume yet, see the Newcomers section.
faq.a3: Registration runs online via Registračka.cz. After filling in the form you’ll get confirmation and payment instructions. Payment must be made within 10 days.
faq.a4: A medic is always present at the event. Combat rules are designed to minimise injury risk. If anything happens, find the nearest organiser.
faq.q5: How much does the event cost?
faq.a5: The fee depends on the date of registration. The current price is in the Registration section.
faq.q6: Can I bring my own weapon?
faq.a6: Only LARP-safe weapons that pass the safety check. Sharp, metal or unsafely hard weapons are not allowed.
